newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates stable ahead of special advances.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates stable ahead of special advances.

text.p: Trade on the Dutch money market was quiet early Monday, with rates unchanged from Friday and no factors to spur activity.
Call money changed hands at 3.15 percent, and dealers said they expected overnight money to trade around the same level on Tuesday, little affected by this afternoon's new special advances pact.
They said they expected the new special advances pact to be pegged at an unchanged rate of 2.90 percent, adding the guilder/mark rate did not justify a rate increase.
The current pact expires on Tuesday and had a relatively short duration of four days.
"They want to monitor the guilder/mark very closely, and they're succeeding," one dealer said.
The Finance Ministry's Agent gave indicative prices for June Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) of 3.10 percent, while December DTCs were set at 3.18 percent, both unchanged from Friday.
Dealers said they did not see much activity in these DTC programmes, as the pricing was not very attractive.
The guilder weakened slightly against the mark, trading at 112.509 per 100 marks, down from 112.49 on Friday.
On Wednesday, the market will be closed for Queen's Day, a Dutch public holiday to mark the Queen's official birthday.
